newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanians turn election equipment to good use.
newsitem.headline: Albanians turn election equipment to good use.

text.p: Albanians quickly found a way to put to good use sophisticated lamps brought in by Western observers to prevent people voting twice in general elections -- they are great at detecting counterfeit bank notes.
"Someone tested two 1,000 lek ($6) notes with the bulb and saw the apparatus could tell which were forged and which were not," the daily Koha Jone said on Thursday.

The lamps, provided by the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe overseeing the election, used fluorescent bulbs able to spot a stamp placed on the left thumb of voters taking ballot papers into polling booths.

Koha Jone said money changers in the southern constituency of Skrapar waited for voting to end in last Sunday's first round of voting in Europe's poorest country and managed to acquire lamps through one means or another.
"Not a single lamp was sent back to the Central Election Commission, not even the spare ones," it said.
